To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of speech recognition and generation in computer systems has been limited to a few applications, but the technology shows promise for telephonebased services.

(1) speech input is useful for hands-busy and eyes-busy tasks, (2) dictation is more accurate than transcription, (3) speech recognition is more difficult for telephone-based services, (4) speech output is more useful for telephone services, (5) dialogue systems are useful for telephone services but not for desktop applications, (6) prosody is important for human-human interaction and not important for human-computer interactions, (7) short-term memory is important
speech recognition and synthesis are useful for certain applications but not for others.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of speech as an input and output modality for interactive computer systems.
the design of human-computer interfaces that are based on spoken input and output.
the design and implementation of speech recognition and generation for human-computer dialogue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of speech recognition in human-computer interaction has been limited to certain applications.
speech is a viable input/output modality for certain applications. It can be used for dictation, hands-free control,
speech recognition is a useful tool for human-computer interfaces but that its use should be restricted to specific applications and environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new theory of human acoustic memory and have shown how to apply it to the development of better human-computer interfaces for speech.
we have demonstrated that speech input can be effective for a variety of tasks and that the technology is now mature enough to make speech input practical.
the human-computer interface is a very broad field, with many different aspects to it, and that it has a great deal to offer in the way of improving the way we use computers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of speech interfaces should be based on an understanding of human speech and the cognitive processes that underlie it.
speech input is a good choice for hands-busy and eyes-busy situations.
the human auditory system can process a lot more information than is currently being used in speech recognition systems.
